summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted from rehabilitation with acute onset substernal chest pain, worse with inspiration and lying flat. Initial concern was for acute coronary syndrome, but serial troponins were negative and EKG changes were nonspecific. The pain pattern and recent CABG suggested pericarditis, though echo showed no effusion. Elevated WBC and new infiltrate on CXR led to diagnosis of pneumonia, treated with IV vancomycin and cefepime. A PICC line was placed for outpatient antibiotic completion. Mild acute on chronic diastolic heart failure was managed with cautious diuresis. Her kidney function worsened slightly but stabilized. Metoprolol was held due to bradycardia and will be restarted at lower dose. She improved clinically, remained pain-free, and was discharged back to extended care with a plan for follow-up and sleep study for suspected OSA.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic heart failure
Diabetes with renal manifestations, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage I through stage IV, or unspecified
